findings.title: A saved continuation from a normally completed request can execute application callbacks after shutdown
related_locations: HttpExecution.java:46-54 removes a completed/idle execution from lifecycle tracking
HttpExecution.java:287-292 saved Next delegates directly to submit
NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/internal/AppLifecycle.java:38-56 shutdown cancels only currently tracked executions
findings.mechanism: submit rejects cancelled/ABORTED only. A normally COMPLETED execution is cleaned and removed from AppLifecycle.executions, so later shutdown never cancels that object. Its retained Continue remains callable and submit establishes a new owner and enters user callbacks without checking the lifecycle closed state. Those callbacks can access services and other app resources already closed during shutdown.
shortest_deterministic_candidate_red: Register GET /x as Middleware: save Next to AtomicReference, send("ok"), return without continuing. Register a downstream middleware that increments a counter.
Complete one request and wait for normal response completion/initial callback return so the execution is removed from lifecycle tracking. Assert downstream counter0.
Call app.shutdown(0, SECONDS) and wait for TERMINATED, then invoke savedNext.run().

Assert downstream counter remains0, no extra access/completion record or resource resurrection. Current source admits the saved continuation and increments the counter. Add a separate RUNNING post-response continuation control so the fix does not restore the prohibited universal completed-response guard.
findings.runtime_evidence: Static implementation finding; candidate Java RED intentionally not executed because this audit forbids builds. Core owner must confirm via TDD.
findings.minimal_fix_direction: Gate new continuation work against the lifecycle terminal cancellation/closed state even after request deregistration, retaining already-owned callback cleanup and valid RUNNING post-response continuation semantics.

findings.title: The global depth64 trampoline changes observable after-next order before the pinned router yields
related_locations: HttpExecution.java:64-78 queued work runs after the current user callback unwinds
findings.mechanism: At depth64 a same-thread Next queues its task and returns, so application after-next statements execute before downstream callbacks. Pinned Express router2.2.0 remains synchronous for65-99 middleware/Route callbacks. It also maintains independent router and Route sync counters; simply changing the one global limit to100 would still mishandle a70-layer+70-Route-callback chain. This can run application cleanup/transaction after-next code before the downstream handler that relies on it.
shortest_deterministic_candidate_red: Register65 normal use callbacks that record before<i>, call Next.run(), then record after<i>; register a final GET /x that records terminal and sends ok.

Send GET /x and await initial callback/all owned work; compare the full trace to the pinned reference. The reference terminal index65 is before after0 index130. Source depth64 queues the terminal before the65th middleware can advance, yielding after0 before terminal.

Add separate65/99/100/101 Route-callback and middleware boundaries and a mixed70-use+70-Route-callback trace to preserve the two independent reference yielding policies; keep the existing1500-callback stack-safety test.
